causal_chain.statement: The stage44 fixture gates only the first SSE body chunk; the common server records the real POST and writes HTTP headers before it awaits any per-chunk gate.
Empty rate-limit headers still produce a default snapshot. This is explicit production behavior and has its own pre-existing empty-header unit case.
spawn_response_stream sends the header-derived RateLimits event before reading the SSE body.
The client mapper forwards other response events, including RateLimits, to the outer stream.
The first outer ResponseEvent closes the recovery arm and gates provider output before the event variant is matched. Durable Ready seen earlier is therefore insufficient to prove current eligibility.

header_helper_search.scope: All codex-rs Rust files at stage44; header_gate|response_gate|gate.*header|header.*gate and start_streaming_sse_server
header_helper_search.result: No existing pre-header gate helper in common; response_gate matches in its callers are per-chunk gates.

ownership_and_cancellation_review: The first queued chunks, their completion sender, and initial_response_gate.take() are selected under one existing state mutex. Later responses receive no initial gate.

take_next_stream returns an owned private StreamingSseResponse; its state guard is dropped when the function returns. The header gate is awaited by the connection handler after this return, with neither queue nor request mutex held.

The raw POST body is recorded and request_notify fired before selecting/awaiting the response gate. Read-only rollout checks continue to observe the actual physical send, not a synthetic request or Ready state.

Dropping the existing gate sender yields Err and returns before headers, chunks, or the completion timestamp are sent. Dropping the owned socket and completion sender reports connection/receipt cancellation; no successful fake response or recovery marker is manufactured.
Gate success continues through the same write_sse_headers, per-chunk gates, body write/flush, completion send, and shutdown as the original helper. Gate=None adds no suspension point before headers.

GET /v1/models, malformed request handling, unknown paths, empty response queue behavior, timeout values, and shutdown ownership remain unchanged. The existing helper does not track every spawned connection task; this candidate does not claim to add that behavior.
